source_refs.note: Cell Membrane: a main subheading of 2.1 Structure of bacteria, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 38-38.

blocks.text: Cell membrane or plasma membrane is present just beneath cell wall. It lies at the outermost in bacteria that lack cell wall (e.g., Mycoplasmas and Sarcoplasmas). The cell membrane of bacteria does not have sterols (e.g., cholesterol) in its chemical makeup. At some points, cell membrane invaginates and forms vesicles, tubules or lamellae in cytoplasm. These structures are known as mesosomes. These are involved in DNA replication and cell division and also serve as respiratory centres.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints “Sarcoplasmas”; there is no group of bacteria by that name. The bacteria that lack a cell wall are mycoplasmas and spiroplasmas, as the book itself says in 2.6 (“Mycoplasmas and Spiroplasmas … lack cell walls”).
